newsitem.title: USA: IMF encouraged by Turkey, but much needs to done.
newsitem.headline: IMF encouraged by Turkey, but much needs to done.

text.p: A senior IMF official said on Thursday he saw a "new willingness" on the part of Turkey to take the action needed to put its economy back on track.
But International Monetary Fund First Deputy Managing Director Stanley Fischer said that much remained to be done.
"There's a generalized willingness to take the right measures but what they are we still have to agree on,' he said, adding, "There is a lot of hard work to be done still."
Economic policymakers from Turkey got together with IMF officials on the fringes of the Fund's joint annual meeting here with the World Bank.

Turkish Prime Minister Necemettin Erbakan said earlier this week in Ankara that his Islamist-led coalition government will draw up a zero-deficit budget for next year which aims to grant real wage hikes to public employees.
Turkish officials there said an IMF team is expected to come to Ankara for talks on a stand-by loan to rescue the country's troubled economy from big public deficits and high inflation.
